meta.name: NeuroPath Synthetic Validation Dataset & KPI Algorithms
meta.description: Synthetic patient profiles and formal KPI algorithms for engineering the NeuroPath analytics engine. Each profile represents a distinct trauma/regulation archetype with 90-day projected recovery trajectories.

demographics.medication: SSRI (sertraline 100mg), prazosin as needed for nightmares

traumaPresentation.polyvagalState: Sympathetic dominance — elevated SNS, suppressed PNS
traumaPresentation.treatmentHistory: 2 years of CBT, partial response; currently in PE therapy

projected90DayTrajectory.interventionProtocol: Coherent breathing (20 min AM + PM) + Trauma-sensitive yoga (3×/week) + Sleep consolidation + Fixed wake time
projected90DayTrajectory.statusAt90Days: Partial recovery — clinically meaningful HRV improvement but not yet normalized (target >40 ms). Maintaining protocol adherence critical.

demographics.condition: Complex PTSD (childhood emotional abuse), dissociative subtype

traumaPresentation.polyvagalState: Dorsal vagal dominance — 'shutdown' state, paradoxical high HRV with low engagement
traumaPresentation.treatmentHistory: 3 years of psychodynamic therapy; current somatic experiencing therapy

projected90DayTrajectory.interventionProtocol: Body scan meditation (15 min AM) + 5-4-3-2-1 grounding (as needed) + Behavioral activation (graduated step increase) + Fixed wake time + Audio gratitude journaling (evening)
projected90DayTrajectory.statusAt90Days: Marked improvement in engagement markers (activity, voice variance, pause ratio). HRV normalizing downward from dissociation baseline toward healthy range (35-45 ms). Interoceptive awareness improving — alexithymia scores reduced by 40%.

traumaPresentation.polyvagalState: Mixed: sympathetic activation at night (sleep anticipatory anxiety), mild hyperarousal during day
traumaPresentation.treatmentHistory: 6 sessions of CBT-I (partial adherence); no prior voice or HRV biofeedback

projected90DayTrajectory.interventionProtocol: Nighttime HRV biofeedback (15 min pre-bed) + Stimulus control therapy + Blue light management + Extended exhale (4-7-8) at bedtime + Sleep consolidation
projected90DayTrajectory.statusAt90Days: Full recovery in sleep metrics (SOL <20 min, efficiency >90%). HRV normalized. No longer using PRN benzodiazepine. Voice markers indicate reduced tension.

demographics.condition: Occupational burnout (ICU nurse, post-COVID), adjustment disorder

symptomProfile: Physical fatigue despite high step count
Poor recovery (HRV doesn't improve with rest)
traumaPresentation.polyvagalState: Sympathetic exhaustion — high sympathetic tone but depleted resources
traumaPresentation.clinicalSeverity: Moderate-severe (MBI: high EE 32, low PA 18, high CY 14)
traumaPresentation.treatmentHistory: 1 month medical leave; no prior biofeedback

projected90DayTrajectory.interventionProtocol: Coherent breathing (10 min AM) + Progressive muscle relaxation (PM) + Sleep consolidation + Fixed wake time + Behavioral activation reduction (deliberate rest) + Mindfulness-based stress reduction
projected90DayTrajectory.statusAt90Days: Good recovery. HRV approaching normal range. Sleep architecture repaired (deep sleep >18%). Energy returning — resting HR dropped 10 bpm. Voice markers show reduced tension.

demographics.condition: ADHD (combined type), emotional dysregulation, mild anxiety

traumaPresentation.polyvagalState: Rapid state-switching between sympathetic (hyperfocus) and ventral vagal (social engagement). Difficulty staying in regulated state.
traumaPresentation.clinicalSeverity: Moderate (ASRS: 18, SDQ emotional dysregulation subscale: high)
traumaPresentation.treatmentHistory: ADHD coaching, currently trialing stimulant medication

projected90DayTrajectory.interventionProtocol: Box breathing (as needed for emotional regulation) + Progressive muscle relaxation (PM) + Fixed wake time (critical for ADHD) + Blue light management + Morning body scan (5 min)
projected90DayTrajectory.statusAt90Days: Improvement in regulation capacity. Speech rate reduced to near-normal. Sleep regularity significantly improved. Emotional reactivity episodes reduced by ~40%. HRV still below optimal but trending positively.

demographics.condition: Post-partum anxiety, sleep fragmentation due to infant care

symptomProfile: Difficulty relaxing even when infant sleeps
traumaPresentation.polyvagalState: Chronic hypervigilance — unable to downshift from sympathetic despite sleep opportunity
traumaPresentation.treatmentHistory: Peer support group; no formal therapy (time constraints)

projected90DayTrajectory.interventionProtocol: Extended exhale (4-7-8, 3-5 min when infant sleeps) + Body scan (5 min, when possible) + Sleep consolidation (align with infant sleep windows) + Audio gratitude journaling (voice check-in, 2 min) + Support partner engagement for sleep shifts
projected90DayTrajectory.statusAt90Days: Moderate improvement. HRV and sleep metrics improving but constrained by infant care demands. Voice markers show reduced anxiety (F0 decreasing). WASO improving as infant sleep consolidates. Realistic expectation: partial recovery until infant sleep matures.

demographics.condition: Fibromyalgia, PTSD (MVA 3 years ago), chronic pain

traumaPresentation.polyvagalState: Severe dysregulation — lowest HRV in cohort, minimal autonomic flexibility. Pain maintains sympathetic activation; sympathetic activation amplifies pain (positive feedback loop).
traumaPresentation.treatmentHistory: Pain management program; 1 year of CBT; aquatic therapy; minimal response

projected90DayTrajectory.interventionProtocol: Trauma-sensitive gentle yoga (15 min, 4×/week, modified for pain) + Coherent breathing (5 min AM, 10 min PM) + Sleep consolidation + Fixed wake time + HRV biofeedback (resonance frequency training, 10 min, 5×/week) + Behavioral activation (pain-contingent, graduated)
projected90DayTrajectory.statusAt90Days: Slower recovery trajectory due to pain-HRV feedback loop. However, HRV improving (16→27 ms), pain scores reduced by 25%. Voice HNR improving indicating reduced vocal strain. Deep sleep still low but trending up. Long-term prognosis good with continued protocol adherence.

demographics.condition: Alcohol use disorder (in recovery, 4 months sober), PTSD (childhood)

symptomProfile: Vivid dreams / nightmares (REM rebound from alcohol cessation)
traumaPresentation.polyvagalState: Sympathetic dominant with REM-related fragmentation. Alcohol had been used as 'chemical vagal activator' — now withdrawn, ANS is raw and unregulated.
traumaPresentation.treatmentHistory: 28-day inpatient detox + IOP; currently in 12-step program; 4 months sober

projected90DayTrajectory.interventionProtocol: Box breathing (acute craving management) + HRV biofeedback (resonance frequency training, 20 min daily) + Sleep consolidation + Stimulus control + Fixed wake time + Behavioral activation (structured daily routine) + Audio gratitude journaling
projected90DayTrajectory.statusAt90Days: Strong recovery. HRV nearly doubled (20→36 ms). REM sleep normalizing (30%→23%). Cravings reduced by 65% (self-report). Sleep architecture largely repaired. Relapse prevention anchored by HRV biofeedback — user reports 'seeing the data helps me not drink.' Voice markers recovering.

demographics.condition: High-functioning generalized anxiety, perfectionism, burnout risk

symptomProfile: Chest tightness / shallow breathing under pressure
Insight: knows stress is unhealthy but feels impossible to change
traumaPresentation.polyvagalState: Generally well-regulated at baseline but easily tipped into sympathetic during work stress. Good autonomic recovery suggests resilience if intervention is preventive.
traumaPresentation.treatmentHistory: Executive coaching, occasional meditation app use (inconsistent)

projected90DayTrajectory.interventionProtocol: Slow-paced breathing (5 min, 2×/day, at transition points) + Box breathing (before high-stakes meetings) + Fixed wake time + Blue light management + Audio gratitude journaling (evening, 3 min) + Optical intervention timing based on HRV dip detection
projected90DayTrajectory.statusAt90Days: Preventive success. HRV optimized (32→42 ms). Speech rate normalized. Reports feeling 'more patient' and 'less reactive.' Voice biomarkers show increased dynamic range — emotional expressiveness improving. Well positioned to maintain.

demographics.condition: Developmental trauma (bullying, parental divorce), school refusal, social anxiety

symptomProfile: School refusal (missed 40% of days in past term)
Avoidance of phone calls / voice communication
traumaPresentation.polyvagalState: Mixed dorsal (shutdown at school trigger) and sympathetic (anticipatory anxiety the night before). Ventral vagal engagement strong with safe people (family, close friends) but collapses in social threat contexts.
traumaPresentation.treatmentHistory: Family therapy (6 sessions); school counselor; no prior wearable or voice intervention

projected90DayTrajectory.interventionProtocol: 5-4-3-2-1 grounding (before school) + Box breathing (morning anxiety) + Behavioral activation (graduated school re-entry with step goals) + Fixed wake time (parent-supported) + Audio gratitude journaling (optional, non-judgmental prompts) + Gamified step goal rewards
projected90DayTrajectory.statusAt90Days: Meaningful improvement. School attendance up from 60% to 85%. Activity levels normalized (1,500→5,500 steps). Voice shimmer decreasing (reduced vocal tension). Parent-report: 'much more willing to talk about feelings.' HRV improving, approaching age-appropriate norms. Protocol gamification was key for compliance.

meta.description: Formal algorithmic definitions for NeuroPath's three business KPIs, plus three supporting metrics. Each includes: formula, window, aggregation method, minimum clinically significant change, and validation criteria.

dataSources.voiceProcessing: On-device Meyda + custom DSP feature extraction (see RESEARCH.md Section 10)
dataSources.interventionLogs: App-side tracking of intervention type, start/end timestamps, user completion status

kpi1.name: Regulation Recovery Rate (3R)
kpi1.businessKpi: Average improvement in physiological markers (e.g., Heart Rate Variability) among active users over 90 days
kpi1.definition: The rate of change in morning HRV (SDNN) over a rolling 90-day window, measured as the slope of the linear regression of daily morning SDNN values.

algorithm.step1: QUERY: Collect all HKQuantityTypeIdentifier.heartRateVariabilitySDNN samples from HealthKit for the user, filtered to samples taken between 05:00-09:00 local time (morning window)
algorithm.step2: AGGREGATE: For each calendar day, compute median SDNN of all morning samples. If fewer than 2 samples exist for a day, mark day as missing.
algorithm.step3: IMPUTE: For missing days (up to 7 consecutive), use linear interpolation between nearest valid neighbors. If > 7 consecutive days missing, truncate the window.
algorithm.step4: OUTLIER: Remove values > 3 standard deviations from the rolling 14-day mean. Replace with clipped value at 3σ boundary.
algorithm.step5: REGRESS: Fit ordinary least squares linear regression: SDNN = β₀ + β₁ × days. The slope β₁ is the raw daily rate of change.
algorithm.step7: SIGNIFICANCE: Report p-value of β₁ coefficient. Flag as significant if p < 0.05.

kpi1.minimumClinicallySignificantChange: 3R > 1.67 ms/month (equivalent to +5 ms over 90 days, per RESEARCH.md Section 7)

validationCriteria.testPass: 3R for P001 (combat veteran) should be ~3.5 ms/month (from 18→35 ms over 12 weeks ≈ +17 ms / 12 weeks × 4 = +5.7 ms/month)
validationCriteria.testBaseline: P007 (fibromyalgia) should show 3R ≈ 2.7 ms/month (from 16→27 ms over 12 weeks ≈ +11 ms / 12 weeks × 4 = +3.7 ms/month)
validationCriteria.testFloor: A user with all SDNN values within ±1 ms should yield 3R ≈ 0 (no significant trend)

kpi2.name: Intervention Efficacy Score (IES)
kpi2.businessKpi: Percentage of suggested interventions that lead to a measurable shift back to a regulated state
kpi2.definition: The proportion of completed intervention sessions where pre-to-post biometrics show a clinically meaningful shift toward parasympathetic regulation.

formula.primaryMetric: IES = (count of sessions with ΔSDNN ≥ +5 ms) / (total completed sessions) × 100

algorithm.step1: DETECT: Identify intervention sessions from app logs (type, start_time, end_time, completion_status = 'completed').
algorithm.step2: PRE: Collect the median SDNN value in the 10-minute window immediately preceding the intervention start.
algorithm.step3: POST: Collect the median SDNN value in the 10-minute window immediately following the intervention end.
algorithm.step5: CLASSIFY: If ΔSDNN ≥ +5 ms (the minimum clinically significant change from RESEARCH.md), mark session as 'positive_shift'. If ΔSDNN < -5 ms, mark as 'negative_shift'. Otherwise 'neutral'.
algorithm.step6: AGGREGATE: IES = (count positive_shift) / (total completed) × 100 over a rolling 30-day window.
algorithm.step7: BY_TYPE: Also compute IES_breathwork, IES_somatic, IES_sleep by filtering to intervention type.
algorithm.step8: VOICE_AUGMENT: If voice biomarker data is available (F0, jitter, HNR), compute a multi-modal shift score: ΔMulti = 0.6 × z(ΔSDNN) + 0.2 × z(ΔHNR) + 0.1 × z(-Δjitter) + 0.1 × z(-ΔspeechRate). Positive ΔMulti ≥ 0.5 indicates multi-modal shift.

kpi2.minimumClinicallySignificantChange: IES improvement > 10 percentage points over a 30-day rolling window indicates protocol effectiveness

validationCriteria.testPass: P003 (insomnia) doing nightly HRV biofeedback: pre-session SDNN ≈ 24, post-session SDNN ≈ 32 → Δ = +8 ms → positive_shift ✓
validationCriteria.testEdge: P002 (dissociative) doing body scan: pre-SDNN 58, post-SDNN 56 → Δ = -2 → neutral. This is correct — dorsal vagal type shouldn't be expected to show HRV increase from meditation in same way.
validationCriteria.testVoice: P004 (burnout) doing coherent breathing: pre-HNR 9.0, post-HNR 10.5 → ΔHNR = +1.5 dB. Combined with ΔSDNN = +6 ms → ΔMulti likely positive

kpi3.name: Retention & Engagement Score (RES)
kpi3.businessKpi: Monthly active users (MAU) and churn rate for both individual and clinician tiers
kpi3.definition: Two-component metric: (1) Active usage ratio — days with ≥1 biometric data upload / total days in period. (2) Churn prediction — probability of user disengaging based on biometric trend and usage patterns.

formula.componentB: RES_churnRisk = sigmoid( β₀ + β₁×(HRV_trend_14d) + β₂×(session_completion_rate) + β₃×(days_since_last_session) + β₄×(step_count_trend) )

algorithm.step1: ACTIVE: For each calendar day, check if user has ANY HealthKit data pushed (HRV, steps, sleep, heart rate). Count days with data vs total days in rolling 30-day window.
algorithm.step2: COMPLETION: Compute session completion rate = (sessions completed) / (sessions started) over rolling 14-day window.
algorithm.step3: HRV_TREND: Compute 14-day linear slope of morning SDNN (same algorithm as KPI-REG-RECOVERY but 14-day window).
algorithm.step5: STEP_TREND: Compute 14-day linear slope of daily step count.
algorithm.step6: CHURN_RISK: Apply logistic regression with coefficients calibrated on historical data. Initial recommended coefficients: β₀ = 0.5, β₁ = -0.15 (positive HRV trend → lower churn risk), β₂ = -0.02 (higher completion → lower risk), β₃ = 0.05 (more days since session → higher risk), β₄ = -0.01 (increasing activity → lower risk).
algorithm.step7: THRESHOLD: If RES_churnRisk > 0.50, trigger retention protocol (personalized nudge, clinician check-in if B2B, adjusted intervention difficulty).

kpi3.minimumClinicallySignificantChange: A 15% improvement in RES_active or a 0.15 decrease in RES_churnRisk over 30 days

validationCriteria.testPass: P005 (ADHD student) with step count 7,200, HRV trend +0.3 ms/day, completion rate 60%, 2 days since session → RES_churnRisk ≈ 0.35 (medium engagement)
validationCriteria.testWarning: P010 (adolescent) with HRV trend flat, completion rate 30%, 7 days since session → RES_churnRisk ≈ 0.65 (churn warning — trigger retention)
validationCriteria.testHigh: P009 (executive) with HRV trend +0.4 ms/day, completion rate 85%, 0 days since session → RES_churnRisk ≈ 0.12 (high engagement)

supportingMetrics.name: Sleep Quality Index (SQI)
supportingMetrics.description: Composite score combining multiple sleep markers into a single 0-100 index for dashboard display.
supportingMetrics.formula: SQI = 0.30 × z(sleep_efficiency) + 0.25 × z(deep_sleep_pct) + 0.15 × z(-sleep_onset_latency) + 0.15 × z(-WASO) + 0.15 × z(sleep_regularity_index), normalized to 0-100

supportingMetrics.name: Autonomic Balance Score (ABS)
supportingMetrics.description: Single-score indicator of autonomic nervous system state, combining HRV, resting HR, and respiratory rate.
supportingMetrics.formula: ABS = 0.50 × z(SDNN) + 0.30 × z(-restingHR) + 0.20 × z(-respiratoryRate), normalized to 0-100. Higher = more parasympathetic / regulated.

supportingMetrics.name: Voice Recovery Score (VRS)
supportingMetrics.description: Composite voice biomarker score indicating vocal relaxation and parasympathetic activation.
supportingMetrics.formula: VRS = 0.35 × z(HNR) + 0.25 × z(-jitter) + 0.20 × z(-shimmer) + 0.10 × z(F0_variance) + 0.10 × z(-speech_rate), normalized to 0-100
